newsitem.title: USA: Median CPI up 0.3 pct in May -- Cleveland Fed.
newsitem.headline: Median CPI up 0.3 pct in May -- Cleveland Fed.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland said its measure of the median Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.3 percent in May, equaling its April rise.
On an annualized basis, median CPI was up 3.1-percent in May, the Cleveland Fed said.
Median CPI is a measure of core inflation calculated from data released in the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly consumer price report.
Earlier on Tuesday, the BLS said CPI rose 0.1 percent in May, just as it did in April. Less food and energy, consumer prices rose 0.2 percent in May after a 0.3-percent gain last month, the BLS said.
Over the past 12 months, median CPI climbed 2.7 percent, CPI advanced 2.3 percent and CPI less food and energy rose 2.5 percent.
